questions.stem: How is the level of thyroxine in the blood controlled?

options.text: By the nervous system sending electrical impulses
By negative feedback involving the pituitary gland
By the amount of food eaten each day

questions.explanation: Thyroxine levels are controlled by negative feedback. When levels are high, the pituitary gland reduces TSH production, which slows thyroxine release. When levels drop, TSH increases.
